title: Soft-commit speculative decode: decoupled scheduler, early-commit metrics, and graceful rollback horizon
creator: Marco Liu
description: Implement a soft-commit speculative decoding flow that separates prefill from decode scheduling, introduces early-commit acceptance metrics, and provides a deterministic rollback horizon for graceful fallback to full decode. This ticket defines the runtime scheduling component, acceptance signals, kernel affinity hints, and a phased rollout plan.
background: We have multiple prototype tickets exploring speculative decode heuristics and prefill probes, but production behavior remains brittle across model/kernel combinations. Current tight-coupled prefill->decode handoff causes tail latency spikes when fallbacks trigger or when kernel selection changes at decode time. Teams need a clearer contract for early-commit decisions and a scheduler that supports soft commits (temporary speculative outputs) with a bounded rollback horizon.
proposal: 1) Introduce a decoupled prefill/decoder scheduler (Soft-Commit Scheduler) that enqueues a lightweight speculative decode on a candidate model variant while allowing the primary decode to continue. 2) Emit an early-commit score composed of token-level logit cosine similarity, prefix-match ratio, and token-entropy delta; score normalizes to [0,1]. 3) Define a rollback horizon (configurable time/token budget) during which speculative outputs are 'soft-committed' and can be replaced by a canonical full-decode result if acceptance score falls below threshold. 4) Kernel-affinity hints: scheduler tags speculative tasks with preferred kernel profile (e.g., int8-packed, transposed-attention) to reduce mode-switch overhead and optimize prefetching. 5) Fallback plan: if acceptance fails inside horizon, abort speculative stream, surface a combined latency-cost delta metric, and run fallback decode using pinned kernel/model variant. 6) Provide telemetry and control knobs in Console to tune acceptance threshold, horizon length, and kernel affinity per customer route.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-Commit Scheduler implemented in runtime with feature flag (enable_spec_soft_commit)
Early-commit score produced for each speculative decode and included in per-request trace
Rollback horizon default = 250ms or 8 tokens (configurable) and enforced by scheduler
Kernel-affinity hinting used to choose candidate kernel and reduces kernel migration events by >=40% in canary
Canary tests show overall P95 latency improves or remains neutral while rollback rate <3% on demo workloads
Console exposes controls: acceptance_threshold (0.0-1.0), rollback_horizon_ms, speculative_model_weight
milestones: Canary rollout to 5% traffic + telemetry collection (Mar 24)
Expand canary to 25% and run cost/regression tests (Apr 1)
Full rollout gated on rollback_rate < 5% and no SLO regressions (Apr 4)
telemetry_metrics: rollback_rate: percentage of speculative outputs replaced within horizon
kernel_migration_count: count of kernel switches per request
extra_compute_cost_speculative: additional token-GPU-time for speculative path
latency_p50/p95/p99 for prefill, speculative-decode, and final-decode
user_visible_regressions: semantic eval delta on curated prompt-set
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Start with internal workloads and non-critical customer test routes. 1) Enable flag + synthetic load test. 2) Canary at 5% traffic for 24h, evaluate telemetry. 3) Expand to 25% for e2e quality/regression checks. 4) If rollback_rate < 5% and no quality regressions, enable globally for targeted model families. Use automatic kill-switch if P99 tail latency increases by >20%.
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler invariants (no lost prefill events, correct horizon enforcement)
Integration test: end-to-end request trace includes early_commit_score and final decision
Performance test: compare P95 latency and kernel migration count with and without soft-commit
Quality test: run curated eval prompt-set to measure semantic drift introduced by speculative outputs
Fault-injection: force kernel failures and ensure fallback path completes successfully
risks: Speculative outputs accepted by downstream services before final decode can cause inconsistent state if not clearly labeled
Mis-calibrated acceptance score could increase user-visible regressions
Kernel affinity hints may increase scheduling fragmentation leading to lower utilization if too conservative
Cost increase from speculative extra work if rollback_rate is high
blockers: GPU driver support for kernel-prefetching and pinning must be validated on dedicated infra
Need upstream telemetry schema change to carry early_commit_score in traces (observability team)
